user.title: Household Calendar Splitter
user.description: Choose the calendars to read events from. You can add people now or later; each person gets a read-only calendar of the events that mention them.

data_description.source_calendars: Existing calendars, e.g. from Google Calendar. They are never changed.
data_description.people: One name per line. Add nicknames and groups afterwards from the integration page.

abort.already_configured: Household Calendar Splitter is already set up.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Household Calendar Splitter is already set up.

data_description.joiner_words: e.g. and, so "Oscar and Felix" means both. Commas, &, + and / always join names.
data_description.leading_words: e.g. with, so "Lunch with Isla" becomes "Lunch" on Isla's calendar.
data_description.strip_names: Off keeps titles exactly as written on every calendar.
data_description.unassigned_name: Events that mention nobody appear on this calendar.
data_description.remove_duplicates: When the same event is on more than one source calendar, show it once on each person's calendar. Shared events still appear on every person they mention.

data_description.name: Shown as the calendar's name. Always recognised in event titles.
data_description.aliases: Nicknames or spellings that also mean this person, e.g. Ozzie.
data_description.case_sensitive: Only match names written exactly as entered, so "Will" matches but "will" does not. Useful when a name is also an ordinary word.

common_word.title: Name is also an everyday word
common_word.description:
{words} is also an ordinary word, so events like "rose ribbon" or "will call" could be put on this person's calendar.

Matching capitalisation exactly avoids most of these. You can also change how names are recognised in the household settings.

data_description.words: Words in an event title that mean this group, e.g. kids or boys.
data_description.everyone: Always includes every person, including people added later.

options.anywhere: Anywhere in the title ("Swim with Oscar")

options.tagged: Only when tagged ("Oscar: swim" or "[Oscar] swim")
